sources.entry: WallpaperMenu - macOS menubar application for navigation through beautiful pictures on the web and set them up as your desktop image.

summary.one_liner: WallpaperMenu is a macOS menubar app for browsing beautiful pictures from the web and setting them as the desktop wallpaper.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes WallpaperMenu as a Mac OS X menubar application that navigates through beautiful pictures on the web and sets them as the desktop image. It is stated to be an unofficial client, not affiliated with any website or service. The current site it accesses is interfaceLIFT.com, and its HTML parsing is isolated in a separate class so that plugins for other wallpaper websites could be added later. The TODO list mentions planned features: configurable download folder and screen resolution, download feedback, and loading placeholders. The README does not describe the interface in detail beyond this.
use_cases: set beautiful web pictures as desktop wallpaper
browse wallpapers from a menubar app on mac
experiment with wallpaper website scraping plugins
stack: Nokogiri (mentioned as desired, not confirmed working)
notable: Menubar app for macOS that fetches wallpapers from the web
HTML parsing isolated in its own class to allow plugins for other picture sites
Currently supports interfaceLIFT.com only, per the README
Unofficial client, not affiliated with the source website
caveats: README says the code is non-production and should not be used yet
Built on MacRuby, an old Ruby implementation for macOS; the README does not give install steps
Several planned features (configurable folder and resolution, download feedback) are still TODO
